subject: Copywriting
subcategory: The Science of Storytelling in Ads
title: Brand Mascots as Characters
description: A quick, practical guide to Brand Mascots as Characters.

hook.text: Tony the Tiger has sold cereal since 1952. The Geico gecko has run since 1999. Characters outlive campaigns by decades.

buildup.text: Leo Burnett pioneered brand mascots. He believed every product has an inherent character waiting to be discovered.

discovery.text: Mascots provide consistency across channels. The character IS the brand in the audience's mind—a living logo.

twist.text: Failed mascots haunt brands. Clippy, the Microsoft paperclip, was so hated it became a symbol of bad UX design.

climax.text: The best mascots have personality, voice, and flaws. They feel like characters, not corporate inventions.

punchline.text: Characters outlive campaigns. Mascots are brand memory.

quiz.question: Who pioneered the use of brand mascots in advertising?
